From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@vanguardhealth.com>, Sam Li <sam.li@vanguardhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Vanguard Health — Dedicated onboarding cadence / validation windows

Alex / Sam — thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Attached is the capacity report we ran against your steady-state traffic sample (vanguard_capacity_report_Q3.pdf) and a draft validation matrix (validation-test-matrix.csv). High level asks and constraints you called out:
- Traffic spike tolerance during batch ETL windows (02:00–04:00 PT)
- Requirement for P95 latency <= 120ms for customer-facing inference calls
- Procurement needs the SOW and redlines for review by 11/16

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Nov 11–12: Redwood runs canary throughput tests against a mirrored slice of your traffic (staging).
2) Nov 13: Joint smoke test (30m) with your infra and our serving team to validate KV cache sizing and prefix cache hit rates.
3) Nov 16: Provide final capacity attestation and SOW for procurement.
4) Nov 20–21: Cutover weekend (non-peak) with rollback window on Nov 21 18:00 PT.

Please confirm the two windows above (canary and smoke) or propose alternatives. I copied Marissa and Karthik for test ownership and Grace for post-cutover support.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@vanguardhealth.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@vanguardhealth.com>, Sam Li <sam.li@vanguardhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vanguard Health — Dedicated onboarding cadence / validation windows

Thanks, Naomi — that looks good as a starting point. A couple of clarifications: 
- The 02:00–04:00 ET ETL window I mentioned is actually EST (our bad) — that maps to 23:00–01:00 PT. Can you ensure canary tests include a simulated ETL spike?
- P95 latency target: our product team will accept 120ms for text generation but wants to see 90th/95th for embedders < 80ms. Are you planning separate instance classes for embedders or a unified pool?

Procurement asked that the SOW include cancellation/termination language and an initial pricing commitment for the first 90 days. Sam (cc'd) is the internal procurement lead — looping him in. We can do the joint smoke on Nov 13 at 10:00 PT if that works for Redwood.

— Alex
Alex Torres
Senior Engineering Manager — AI Platform
Vanguard Health
alex.torres@vanguardhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@vanguardhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vanguard Health — Dedicated onboarding cadence / validation windows

Alex — quick answers inline:
- ETL spike: yes, we'll model the ETL traffic as a 2.5x burst over baseline for a 10-minute sliding window and run it at the canary stage. We'll capture cold-starts and KV cache warmup behavior.
- Embedding latency: we recommend a small dedicated pool for embedders (bfloat16 quant) separate from text-gen workers — helps keep P95 for text stable while giving embedders better tail latency. That's what we used for Brightlane and it worked well.

Operational plan notes for Naomi / Marissa:
- Canary scope (Nov 11–12): 12h run against mirrored traffic, collect P50/P95/P99, per-model KV hit rate, and OOM/eviction metrics.
- Smoke test (Nov 13 10:00 PT): 30m acceptance script (link in drive) — responsible owners: Karthik (runtime), Marissa (traffic mirroring), Alex (validation sign-off).
- Cutover weekend (Nov 20–21): we will stage traffic in 10% increments every 45 minutes with automated rollback on error thresholds (see validation-test-matrix.csv).

I'll prep the canary playbook tonight and attach an initial runbook. Grace will handle post-cutover observability checks.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — summary and mutual action plan below. Please reply with a single-line ACK so procurement can proceed with the SOW.

Mutual action plan (final):
- Nov 11–12: Canary run (Redwood) — deliverables: throughput/latency CSV + attachment with KV hit heatmap. Owner: Karthik.
- Nov 13 10:00 PT: Joint smoke test (30m) — acceptance: P95 gen <=120ms, embed P95 <=80ms, no OOMs. Owner: Alex to sign off.
- Nov 16: SOW+redlines submitted to procurement. Owner: Naomi.
- Nov 20–21: Cutover weekend; staged traffic increments with automatic rollback on threshold breach. Owner: Marissa + Runtime on-call.

Open items:
- Naomi to update SOW with requested cancellation clause and 90-day pricing commitment (target 11/15 EOD).
- Alex to confirm procurement review timeline and whether November 16 is acceptable.

Action: please ACK in a reply to this thread by EOD 11/12. If I don't hear back, Grace will run a dry-run of the observability checks on 11/13 08:00 PT.

Thanks — Naomi
